label: Reflexive distinct-nonmutual dependence separates from asymmetric dependence in two finite models
paraphrase: Mathematical controls on the two Booleans true and false. With D x y iff x = y, D is reflexive and nonmutual on distinct beings but not asymmetric. With D x y iff x = y or (x = true and y = false), D is moreover transitive and has a distinct edge (true depends on false), and it is still not asymmetric. Formal interpretations only: they show the two premises differ in meaning on the diagonal, not which beings depend on which.
